# Synthetic RTI fixtures

Generated locally from Apple's installed tvOS 27.0 simulator, build 24J360,
using `RTIInputSystemDataPayload.updateData` with fresh synthetic
`RTIDocumentState`, `TIDocumentState`, `RTIDocumentTraits`, and
`RTITextOperations` objects. No actual device text, identifiers, or credentials
were captured. The UUID and text in these files are fixed test values.

`state` contains the native document class records. `insert` encodes `ä🎵`.
The same runtime decoded the former CleanFrame classless state archive as
nil session/document; adding document classes and the native scalar fields
made the synthetic candidate decode as NSUUID / RTIDocumentState /
TIDocumentState. This is runtime schema evidence, not proof of a completed
Companion exchange with an iPhone or of all iOS 27 text-edit variants.

`replace` encodes synthetic insertion `ä🎵` with replacement range (0, 1),
generated with `RTITextOperations.insertText:replacementRange:`. Its
`selectionRangeToAssert` must be rejected until replacement is supported;
treating it as an append would corrupt the focused text.

`untargeted` uses a nil RTITextOperations target plus an explicit payload
sessionUUID; Apple's payload decoder preserves the nil target. The envelope
UUID therefore is not silently substituted for an edit target. `input-source`
uses RTIInputSourceState on a targeted operation. Both are synthetic native
archives and support structural diagnostics, not assumptions about real iOS
packets. Target-less edits remain rejected; targeted input-source metadata can
be acknowledged without changing text after the class/type checks below.

`source-version-zero-edit` and `source-version-one-edit` were generated by
feeding the actual CleanFrame Rust state archive (synthetic UUID and Probe)
through RTIInputSystemDataPayload.payloadWithData:version: and then
RTIInputSystemSourceSession.handleTextActionPayload:. Version 0 left the source
session UUID, document state, and newly created operation target nil. Version 1
populated the matching UUID and operation target. Appending synthetic ä🎵 to
the source session's own TIKeyboardOutput generated these two edit archives.
The same result holds with the full Apple-generated state (including traits).
This establishes why the Companion envelope must carry `_tiV: 1` alongside
`_tiD`; a raw archive that independently decodes correctly is insufficient.
Companion's version key is also used by the primary pyatv client implementation:
https://github.com/postlund/pyatv/blob/master/pyatv/protocols/companion/api.py
No fallback for target-less edits is enabled.

`metadata`, `insert-metadata` and `delete-metadata` come from native
RTITextOperations with RTIInputSourceState plus multilingualLanguages NSArray.
Objective-C runtime property metadata confirms those two declared classes.
They are non-text metadata, ignored only after class/array-element validation;
all operations still require an exact target session. Metadata-only becomes an
unchanged edit, which the host acknowledges without an IME write.

Native RTIInputSystemSession.applyLocalTextOperations:toDocumentState: was
exercised on synthetic abc, aä, a🎵, ae+combining-acute, family ZWJ, flag and
skin-tone emoji, and empty strings with deletionCount 1/2/3. It removes extended
grapheme clusters and clamps at empty. Combined deletion+insertion deletes first
and inserts second. TIDocumentState.documentStateAfterDeletingBackward agrees.
The Rust implementation uses unicode-segmentation 1.13.3 (MIT/Apache-2.0), not a
custom Unicode splitter; regressions include the exact native results.
